Flame in a Fireball – NASA

Introduction

A fireball is a very bright meteor that enters the Earth's atmosphere from outer space. According to NASA, fireballs are brighter than ordinary meteors and can sometimes shine even brighter than the full Moon. They are formed when small space rocks, called meteoroids, travel through Earth's atmosphere at very high speeds.
